title: Fall back to the cached price without losing the pool

blocks.text: A product page shows a price from the supplier's pricing API, asked on a pool that every product page shares. When the supplier is slow, the page is meant to show the last price we cached rather than wait. Last month the supplier stopped answering for one product line. Its pages showed the cached prices for a few minutes, as designed, and then every product page on the site, including those of other product lines, started showing cached prices too.
`priceOf(...)` already asks the supplier. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/PriceService.java`:

items: `priceOrCached(...)`: what the page gets back from the call it started.

blocks.text: When you're done, a page shows the supplier's price if it comes within the budget and the cached price otherwise, a supplier that fails gets the cached price too, and a supplier that stops answering doesn't keep the pool's threads from the pages after it. About eight lines in total.
The tests run the pages on a real one-thread pool. Their supplier gives up when its thread is interrupted, as `HttpClient.send` does.

cases.says: a supplier that answers within the budget sets the price the page shows
a supplier that never answers gets the cached price shown once the budget is spent
after the budget runs out, the stuck supplier call is interrupted and its pool thread serves the next page
a supplier call that fails gets the cached price shown

origin.section: A Timed get() Ends the Wait, Not the Task

concepts: A timed get() that runs out ends only the caller's wait; the task keeps its pool thread until cancel(true) interrupts a task that answers interrupts.
